_note: What `the checks pass` means here. Read by .claude/hooks/_projectchecks.py, which the auto-commit gates on and which /verify calls, so the two can never disagree. Each key takes a command string, a list of commands, or false to disable that check as a stated decision. An absent key means detect it.
_why_lint: ruff.toml selects E,F,I,B,S,UP -- the S set is bandit's rules native to ruff, so shell=True is caught without a second tool. Enabling it on 2026-08-03 found four unused imports in shipped hooks. The JSON check is listed explicitly because a configured list REPLACES detection; it is here rather than in a test suite because a stray comma in settings.json silently turns the whole hook layer off.
_why_test: Every executable suite in the repository runs as the test tier, so `--require-test` distinguishes real evidence from a disabled check. No count is stated here on purpose -- the last one said eleven while there were seventeen, and a number nothing enforces is a number that rots.
_why_typecheck_absent: Absent, not false: detection finds mypy.ini and runs it. It was disabled on the assumption an unannotated codebase would drown in findings -- measured instead, it was six errors across nineteen files, all one pattern, all real. A fresh clone without mypy installed skips the check with a note rather than failing.
_why_build: The slow tier resolved ZERO checks until 2026-08-08, and `run_checks --tier slow` printed `PASS: no checks detected` -- a green that asserted nothing about a tier whose whole job is proving the artifact works. This is its first real member: it builds the wheel, reads the built zip rather than the config that produced it, installs it into a clean venv and then into a fresh repo, and requires THAT repo's own tier to come back green. Slow tier and not fast because it creates two virtualenvs; the fast tier gates every auto-commit and must stay in seconds.
_why_smoke: tools/smoke.py is the only check that starts a process, and it had never been exercised by anything. This boots a real server that answers 503 for three seconds and then 200, which is the exact shape the fix addresses: the poll loop treated ANY response as the answer, so a warming backend behind a proxy failed at second one with the whole timeout unspent. Slow tier because it spawns processes and binds ports.
_why_audit_restored:
RESTORED 2026-08-08. This key was `false`, carrying its own instruction: 'restore a real command the moment this repo has a dependency tree worth auditing'. That moment arrived when pyproject.toml declared `pyyaml>=6`. A disabled audit on a repo that ships a dependency is the absent gate that still reads as coverage.
Three shapes were tried before this one, and each failure is the reason for the next: the `pip-audit` console script reported 'tool missing' while the package was installed, because its Scripts/ directory is not on PATH here -- a lookup failure wearing the costume of an environment fact. `--disable-pip` is rejected unless paired with -r. `--strict` audits the whole ENVIRONMENT and failed on a local `clip (1.0)` that is not this project's dependency at all. `pip_audit .` resolves the project's own declared tree, which is the only surface this repository is responsible for.
_why_no_slop_scopes: Two scopes, both explicit. `layer` because THIS repository is the layer, so sweeping .claude/ is sweeping the product -- everywhere else that is the wrong default, which is why the script's own default is now `repo`. `portability` asks whether the layer is safe to install elsewhere, and it was never run by anything until 2026-08-08: it failed with seven dated claims the moment it was, each a sentence that is false in any repository but this one. A gate nothing invokes is not a gate.
